All operations during the specified `makepkg` commands are limited to downloading and extracting prebuilt binaries and auxiliary files.

No obfuscated code, dynamic code evaluation (e.g., `eval`, `base64` decoding), or data exfiltration attempts are present in the global scope. The potentially sensitive operations (like setting SUID bits) occur only within the `package()` function, which is skipped due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. </details>

The use of symlinks to system resources (e.g., hunspell, hyphen, NSS certificates) improves integration and security by leveraging system-managed data instead of relying on outdated or tampered bundled versions.

There are no signs of malicious behavior such as unauthorized network requests, obfuscated code, data exfiltration, or execution of external scripts. All actions are confined to packaging and system integration tasks typical for an AUR binary package.
